clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old male presented with sudden onset seizures and multiple CNS lesions with peripheral contrast enhancement on MRI indicating pyogenic or neoplastic nature. Initial infectious and neoplastic etiologies were considered due to positive serology for Entamoeba histolytica and relevant past history. Brain biopsy revealed histiocytic granulomatous tissue with a prominent IgG4-producing plasma cell infiltrate (IgG4/IgG ratio of 45%, IgG4 >10/HPF), leading to a working diagnosis of IgG4-related disease with no other infectious or neoplastic lesions identified. Exclusion of infections and malignancy was supported by negative CSF cultures, PCR testing, and unremarkable tumor markers and autoimmunity tests. Subsequent steroid treatment resulted in clinical improvement, confirming the diagnosis.
